Package com.github.crittscott.somebuckets.item

Class JBItem

java.lang.Object
net.minecraft.world.item.Item
com.github.crittscott.somebuckets.item.JBItem
All Implemented Interfaces:
VariableStackItem, net.minecraft.world.flag.FeatureElement, net.minecraft.world.level.ItemLike
Direct Known Subclasses:
TBItem
public class JBItem extends net.minecraft.world.item.Item implements VariableStackItem
FIFO storage for item-stack entries and the shared interaction base for Junk and Trash Buckets. Contents live on the bucket stack, compatible entries merge before new entries are allocated, and every intake path applies canStore(ItemStack) before mutation.

    • canStore

      public static boolean canStore(net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack stack)
      The single gate on what these buckets accept.

      Content is not inspected: a container item is refused whether it is empty or full. Junk and Trash Buckets opt out of container nesting (see canFitInsideContainerItems()) so storage never recurses, and portable containers from other mods stay out even when they leave the vanilla flag set.

      Parameters:
      stack - candidate stack
      Returns:
      false when the stack is empty, opts out of container nesting via Item.canFitInsideContainerItems(), is a bundle or shulker box, carries a vanilla inventory component, or exposes a loader item-inventory handler; true otherwise

      protected void playIntakeSound(net.minecraft.world.level.Level level, net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player)
      Plays this bucket's intake feedback at the acting player's position.

    • useOn

      public net.minecraft.world.InteractionResult useOn(net.minecraft.world.item.context.UseOnContext context)
      On a sneak-use against a block, ejects the oldest stored stack into the space adjacent to the clicked face. A non-sneaking use passes so the block's own interaction still runs. Client-side play is prediction; the server authorizes the release and adds the dropped item.
      Overrides:
      useOn in class net.minecraft.world.item.Item

    • interactLivingEntity

      public net.minecraft.world.InteractionResult interactLivingEntity(net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack bucket, net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player, net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity target, net.minecraft.world.InteractionHand hand)
      Feeds a target animal from stored food. The client swaps a one-count probe of the stored food into the hand so vanilla interaction predicts the feedback without touching bucket contents; the server runs the authorized feeding and consumes one stored item when the interaction takes it.

    • canFeed

      public boolean canFeed(net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack bucket, net.minecraft.world.entity.animal.Animal animal)
      Reports whether the animal has stored food and can benefit from it on this activation.
      Parameters:

    • feedAnimal

      public boolean feedAnimal(net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack bucket, net.minecraft.world.entity.animal.Animal animal, @Nullable net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player feeder, net.minecraft.world.InteractionHand hand, ProtectionContext context, net.minecraft.core.Direction face)
      Attempts one authorized feeding action with matching stored food.

      A real feeder delegates to the animal interaction so vanilla or modded behavior decides the outcome and item consumption. A null feeder represents dispenser automation: it applies vanilla's baby-growth or adult-love outcome directly and consumes one stored food item.

      Parameters:
      bucket - the bucket stack
      animal - animal to feed
      feeder - acting player, or null for dispenser automation
      hand - hand used to present the probe food
      context - authorization identity
      face - face associated with the interaction
      Returns:
      true iff the animal interaction consumed the action, not merely because a food candidate existed
